title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-11
content:
Summary:
- Short: since 2026-02-27 deploy, average tokens/sec on prod pool-gamma dropped ~30% for 8k context workloads. P95 latency increased from ~220ms -> ~420ms. Erroring not widespread (few 5xx), but throughput regression obvious in aggregate metrics and customer complaints.

Hypothesis notes (quick):
1) Batching scheduler mis-configured: a change in default max_batch_wait_ms or max_batch_size in commit PR #842 might have increased wait times for batches or forced tiny batches.
2) KV cache invalidation / prefix-caching regression: cache misses cause more decoder compute per request and longer seq len read overhead.
3) Kernel selection fallback: runtime logs show "falling back to generic kernel" for some attention kernels for longer sequences (maybe due to new cuBLAS/cuDNN or driver mismatch).
4) Autoscaling/placement pressure: pods are healthy but GPU utilization lower than before (wasted cycles due to small batch sizes).

Repro steps to capture current state (commands & outputs):
- Check recent deploys: git/log
  git log --oneline --graph --decorate origin/main..HEAD | sed -n '1,20p'
  -> PR #842 (batching defaults change), #847 (kv-cache GC tweak) were merged 2026-02-26

- Live metrics (prom queries used):
  // tokens/sec (pool-gamma) over last 48h
  sum(rate(runtime_tokens_generated_total{pool="pool-gamma"}[5m]))
  -> pre-deploy ~ 18k tps; post-deploy ~12.5k tps

  // batch size distribution
  histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(batching_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  -> median batch size dropped from ~16 -> ~6

- Pod-level logs (example):
  kubectl -n serving logs runtime-gamma-5 -c runtime | sed -n '1,200p'
  ...
  [2026-03-02T03:12:14.312Z] INFO batching: created batch id=337 delay_ms=45 size=4 target_size=16
  [2026-03-02T03:12:14.317Z] WARN scheduler: batch_wait exceeded max_batch_wait_ms=50 -> flushing smaller batch
  [2026-03-02T03:12:14.318Z] INFO runtime: selected kernel attention_legacy (fallback) for layer 10 seq=8192
  [2026-03-02T03:12:14.580Z] INFO kvcache: miss prefix=customer-123 request=abcd

- Example client trace (curl) to reproduce latency spike:
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"model":"rwd-8k", "input":"<~4k tokens prompt>", "max_tokens":512}' -w "\nHTTP %{http_code} - time_total %{time_total}s\n"
  -> HTTP 200 - time_total 0.48s  (was ~0.22s pre-deploy)

- Profiler snapshot (nsys capture on one affected node):
  nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --output=prof-gamma-20260302 ./run-synthetic.sh
  -> kernel timeline shows more small-kernel invocations and lower achieved occupancy; more time in memory-bound kernels.

- GPU metrics via nvidia-smi + DCGM:
  nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1
  -> GPU util per-card: 48% avg (was ~78% before); SM efficiency drops on cards handling longer-seq requests.

What we changed recently (from PRs):
- PR #842: change default batching config: max_batch_wait_ms from 20 -> 50, max_batch_size soft target lowered from 16 -> 12 (intended to reduce tail latency for small prompts).
- PR #847: aggressive KV cache GC (reduce memory pressure), introduced a new cache header serialization format.
- Infra: upgrade CUDA driver on pool-gamma nodes to 12.3.1 around same time.

Quick experiments run so far:
1) Rollback batching defaults (locally in staging): set max_batch_wait_ms=20, max_batch_size=16 -> staging tokens/sec recovered to within 95% of baseline.
   - Command: kubectl -n staging set env deployment/runtime BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS=20 BATCH_TARGET_SIZE=16
2) Disable new KV cache GC (force old code path) -> small improvement in p95 but not full recovery.
3) Force kernel selection to prefer optimized kernels (experimental flag): RUNTIME_FORCE_OPT_KERNEL=1 -> slight improvement, but still below baseline.
4) Revert CUDA driver on one node to 12.2.0 -> that node's tasks show improved SM efficiency; but cluster-wide we still see regression.

Interim conclusion:
- Highest correlation: drop in median batch size (from ~16 to ~6) after PR #842. Smaller batches explain much of the tokens/sec drop and lower GPU utilization. However, commit intended to reduce latency for small prompts — it changed flushing behavior and batch wait threshold, which seems to be flushing early when a mix of short+long requests present.
- KV cache GC / serialization change (PR #847) likely exacerbates CPU-side request overhead (cache misses + serialization) and may increase per-request latency, but is not primary throughput driver.
- Driver/kernel differences likely contribute to worst-case p95 and kernel fallback logs; but the larger effect is batching policy.

Next steps (actionable):
- Roll back PR #842 in prod quickly for pool-gamma and monitor tokens/sec and p95. (Hotfix plan written in linked ticket ENG-1257).
- If rollback recovers metrics, schedule a safer rollout: add canary that measures batch size distribution + tokens/sec and auto-roll if median batch size < 12.
- Add more telemetry: emit per-batch target_size vs actual_size and batch_flush_reason (timeout/target/full). Add histogram of batch_wait_ms.
- Re-run kernel selection tests with both CUDA 12.2 and 12.3; pin driver on pool-gamma to known-good if rollback doesn't fully recover.
- Revert KV cache serialization change in staging and compare CPU overhead per request.

Notes / TODOs:
- [ ] Postmortem template fill (assign: Maya)
- [ ] Add flag to batcher: debug_dump_recent_batches -> dump last 1k batch events for 1 minute (for incident window)
- [ ] Customer outreach: notify affected customers (CS draft in linked Confluence)

Incidental logs / snippets for future debugging:
- "batching: flushing batch id=512 reason=timeout elapsed_ms=52 target_size=16 actual=3"
- "scheduler: backpressure applied: queue_len=1200"
- "kvcache: serialization mismatch: legacy header detected, falling back to slow deserializer"

If I don't get to prod rollback before EOD, leave a short note in #incidents channel and tag @on-call.

Signed-off-by: Ravi Patel
